title: Orchestrated load-shedding, region-aware circuit breaker tuning, and on-call orchestration playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: We need a coordinated, region-aware approach to degrade safely under overload while minimizing noisy pages. This ticket defines target SLO-aligned circuit breaker thresholds, progressive load-shedding policies, and a compact on-call orchestration playbook with automation hooks so that incidents are handled consistently and with minimal manual toil.

Background: Over the last 6 months we've seen two classes of incidents: (1) sudden model-side token surges that saturate GPU queues in a single region and (2) multiregion `soft` degradations where tail latency drifts past SLOs but raw error rates remain low. Current paging rules trigger at single-signal thresholds (p99 latency OR queue depth) leading to noisy pages and inconsistent mitigations. We need a more deterministic policy that leverages signal composition, traffic-class awareness, and automated mitigations before engaging full human escalation.

Goals:
- Define a composite trip condition for circuit breakers (region-aware) that reduces false positives by 60% and reduces pages on noisy events by 50%.
- Implement progressive shedding policies by route/priority (interactive vs batch vs telemetry) that maintain critical-sla traffic while rejecting or delaying lower-priority requests.
- Standardize an on-call orchestration playbook with explicit automated remediation steps (scoped to safe ops) and clear escalation boundaries.
- Provide observability: dashboards, runbook-linked alerts, and post-incident report template.

Acceptance Criteria: (see acceptance_criteria field)

High-level approach:
1) Signal composition and thresholds: define a quorum of three signals to trip a circuit in a region: (A) p99 generation latency > 750ms for > 3m, (B) GPU queue depth > 85% of configured capacity for > 2m, (C) client-visible 5xx rate > 0.8% over 3m OR token drop events > 0.2%. Only when two of three are true do we mark the region "degraded" and begin automated remediation. Threshold values are provisional and will be tuned in staging.

2) Progressive load-shedding: implement a three-tier shedding policy in the request gateway:
  - Tier 0 (critical): health-checks, internal telemetry, and paid SLA routes; never rejected by shedding (can be delayed).
  - Tier 1 (interactive): best-effort; apply graceful degradation (reduce max tokens, lower model family if available, queue with short timeout).
  - Tier 2 (bulk/async/low-priority): immediate 429 with structured Retry-After and shed to background queue or lower-cost variant.
Shedding decisions can be token-aware (long requests more likely to be shed) and per-customer (opt-in per account policy to protect high-value customers).

3) Region failover and circuit fallback: when a region is marked degraded we will:
  - First, activate local shedding policy and spin up preferential routing to other healthy capacity in same region (lighter models) if available.
  - If composite signals persist for 6 minutes, run automated cross-region rerouting policy: upweight healthy region endpoints and start warm-up of spare capacity in target region. Failover is graceful (weight shifting over 60s windows) to avoid cascading load.

4) On-call orchestration playbook (compact):
  - Triage: verify alerts on SRE dashboard, confirm composite signals and affected customer routes.
  - Automated remediations (run automatically on composite trip unless a safety gate is tripped): clear stale worker KV caches, rotate GPU worker pools for the endpoint (github.com/redwood-inference/infra/actions/rotate-gpu-pools), and run model-eviction grace windows.
  - If automated remediation fails after 2 attempts or health does not improve by 10% p99, escalate to human (on-call) for manual steps (scale capacity, initiate cross-region traffic shift).
  - Communication: update incident channel template (links below), mark affected customers via status.redwood.ai/incidents placeholder, and update ticket with mitigation steps.

5) Alerting and paging tuning:
  - Replace single-signal pages with a two-tier alert set:
     * Warning alerts (no page by default, sent to paging-suppressed Slack channel): triggered by single-signal anomalies.
     * Escalation pages: triggered by composite trip condition.
  - Implement automatic page de-duplication and contextual summary payload (top-3 impacted routes, p99 deltas, relevant GitHub PRs) to reduce cognitive load.

6) Automation & safety: all automated remediations must run under a safety gate (no cross-region failover if DB replication lag > 60s or if security_review_required flag for the tenant is true). We will maintain an audit trail for all automated actions.

Trade-offs considered:
- Conservative tripping reduces pages but increases time-to-detect real regressions. We accept a small increase in detection time (target < 2 minutes additional) in exchange for 50% fewer noisy pages.
- Progressive shedding may increase visible 429s for low-priority traffic. We will monitor customer complaints and create shielding policies for high-value customers.

Next steps: build the composite signal engine (ENG-62545), add shedding hooks to the gateway (ENG-62546), author the lightweight playbook and automation jobs (this ticket), and run a fault-injection campaign in staging (ENG-62547).
acceptance_criteria: Composite circuit trip uses >=2 of 3 signals (p99, queue depth, error/token-drop) and reduces noisy pages by >=50% in canary rollout.
Gateway exposes token-aware shedding API and supports per-route priorities with at least two configurable tiers.
Automated remediation jobs (rotate GPU pools, clear KV cache) execute under safety gates and log actions to audit stream.
On-call playbook exists in Confluence with step-by-step checks, quick rollback actions, and escalation windows; playbook reviewed and approved by SRE leads.
Dashboards updated: per-region composite health, shed rate by route, page counts before/after tuning; and a post-deploy runbook test scenario passes in staging.
